questions.question: What happens to data in an H2 in-memory database when the application stops?
options: It is saved to a file called data.sql
It is lost, because it lived only in RAM
It stays until the computer restarts
questions.explanation: In-memory mode keeps tables in RAM only, so everything disappears with the application.

questions.question: Which JDBC URL keeps H2 data on disk so it survives a restart?
questions.explanation: The file mode URL stores the database in files, while the mem mode keeps it in RAM.

questions.question: In the cafe app, data.sql inserts three rows and defer-datasource-initialization is true. How many items does GET /menu return?
options: One, because only the last insert runs
An error, because the table does not exist
questions.explanation: Hibernate creates the table first, then data.sql runs, so all three rows are there.

questions.question: data.sql fails with Table MENU_ITEM not found at startup. What is the most likely fix?
options: Set spring.jpa.defer-datasource-initialization=true so Hibernate creates tables first
questions.explanation: By default data.sql can run before Hibernate builds the tables, so the order must be changed.

questions.question: The developer enables the H2 console with a property but gets a 404 in Spring Boot 4. What is missing?
options: The spring-boot-h2console library on the classpath
questions.explanation: Spring Boot 4 moved the H2 console into its own library, so it must be added as a dependency.
